C-DROPBOX-SAVE-LOAD.Summary: Investigate the reported Safari Dropbox consent failure, make authorization recoverable, and add real Dropbox save/load actions directly to records using s and l.
C-DROPBOX-SAVE-LOAD.Problem: Safari fails after consent at Dropbox's authorize_submit page. The application correctly starts the documented PKCE code flow, but cannot observe browser-side errors or conveniently restart authorization. Its token requests only account access, there is no Dropbox snapshot adapter, and l currently pages right.

Goals.Goal: Narrow down the Safari failure using its full error text and verified Dropbox documentation; correct any demonstrated application defect without claiming to repair an unconfirmed browser or Dropbox failure.
Make sign-in recoverable through a fresh authorization attempt, an accessible manual authorization URL, and an optional browser override.
Add s to save local exercises, sets, and optional preferences to Dropbox, and l to load that saved snapshot into the local application.
Document save/load in records hints and help without restoring Preferences or Sync screens.

Constraints.Constraint: Keep S256 PKCE, offline access, verified account IDs, masked code input, encrypted credentials, staged questionnaire completion, cancellation, and zero writes for fully skipped setup.
Request account_info.read, files.content.read, and files.content.write. Explain configuration of these permissions and reauthorization for accounts linked before file scopes were requested.

The authorize_submit URL belongs to Dropbox's consent page; its /1 prefix alone is not evidence of an obsolete application endpoint. Do not replace the supported manual-code flow with a mandatory callback configuration without evidence that this addresses the reported error.

Provide a fresh sign-in retry from the code step and keep the complete authorization URL accessible on compact screens. Allow DROPBOX_BROWSER to choose a browser, launched with structured arguments and no shell evaluation. Preserve the default browser when no override is set.
s and l act only from records. Preserve gs/ge focus, dialog text, help-owned input, and setup input. Reserve l for load and retain right-arrow, Page Down, f, and Space for next-page navigation.

Use a versioned JSON snapshot at /trainlog.json within the linked app's Dropbox access boundary. Save replaces this remote snapshot. Load replaces local exercises, sets, and preferences with the snapshot atomically; preserve local identities and credentials.

Represent missing preferences explicitly, so saving defaults does not insert a preferences row and loading a snapshot without preferences restores their absence. Validate every loaded model through domain constructors, IDs, unique names, references, weights, timestamps, and supported schema version before applying any local writes.

Use the most recently linked Dropbox account deterministically. Decrypt credentials only inside the adapter, refresh expired access tokens through the public-client refresh flow, and encrypt updated tokens before persistence. Never put identities, keys, or credentials in the remote snapshot.

Run transfers asynchronously with bounded requests and payload sizes. Display progress, success, missing-account/backup, permission, and network failures without blocking terminal input or exposing sensitive response bodies. Avoid overlapping transfers and unsafe edits while a restore is in progress.
On failure, retain local data and browsing state. On successful load, refresh records and units from persistence and retain selected IDs where available, clamping pagination after changed data.
Do not run a live account authorization, upload, download, or modify the real user database during development verification. Preserve inherited uncommitted changes and descriptive repository naming.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Additional providers, automatic/background synchronization, conflict merging, or separate settings/sync screens.
Guaranteeing that a code change fixes Safari connectivity or a Dropbox consent-page failure without reproduction evidence.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The full Safari error is recorded when supplied, and findings distinguish demonstrated application defects from external browser/provider behavior. Authorization URLs and token payloads match the official Dropbox contract.
Authorization requests file read/write permissions, supports fresh retries and an optional browser override, and exposes a usable full URL when the browser cannot finish sign-in.

s exports all exercises and sets plus optional preferences to /trainlog.json using real Dropbox upload. l downloads, validates, and restores this snapshot atomically while preserving local identity credentials.

Save/load work after token expiry through refresh, and handle missing accounts, missing snapshots, denied scopes, malformed data, transport errors, and persistence failures without partial restores or secret leakage.
l triggers load rather than pagination; gs still focuses sets. Dialog/help/setup input cannot trigger transfers. Records and help show l - load and s - save.

Temporary SQLite tests cover complete round trips, absent preference preservation, validation rejection, transaction rollback, and successful UI refresh. Injected HTTP/browser tests cover upload/download/refresh and authorization retry without real user data.
Full Go tests, vet, normal snapshot verification, and selected GRACE final assertions pass after approved implementation.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Injected browser/HTTP tests verify PKCE scopes, retry, safe browser arguments, refresh, upload/download, and sanitized errors.

Temporary database tests verify snapshots, optional preferences, validation, and atomic restores. TUI tests verify shortcut isolation, retained navigation, progress, and successful refresh; intended snapshots are reviewed.

Assumptions.Assumption: The requested save/load actions mean Dropbox backup and full restore. Restore replaces local workout data rather than merging conflicts.
Dropbox consent failure root cause remains unconfirmed until the full Safari error or reproduction evidence is available.
The user explicitly approved this specification, the sequential execution outline, and execution on 2026-10-10. Prior authorization to archive completed GRACE work remains in effect.
